newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: U.S. Scott group takes over Austrian Blizzard.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Scott group takes over Austrian Blizzard.

text.p: U.S. sports giant Scott has acquired Austrian ski maker Blizzard for an undisclosed sum from savings bank Raiffeisenverband Salzburg, the bank said in a statement on Friday.
Raiffeisenverband Salzburg said the deal, effective October 1, should secure production and jobs at Blizzard's Mittersill plant in western Austria.
Blizzard employs 320 in Mittersill and will produce around 250,000 pairs of skis and 100,000 snowboards this year.
"Raiffeisenverband Salzburg is convinced that in Scott it has selected the best partner for (Blizzard's) future," the bank's general director Manfred Holztrattner said.

Scott, which employs 600 worldwide and has a turnover of around 2.6 billion schillings ($243 million), will combine the distribution and marketing of Blizzard and Scott products in Austria and Germany -- including Scott skiing and cycling equipment, Hooger snowboards, Schwinn fitness equipment and Yeti bikes.

"A production site in Europe will help snowboard maker Hooger to develop. Our strategy is to build a strong, global market position in snowboarding. We will also try to further the Blizzard name," Scott president Tom Stendahl said.

The acquisition will boost Hooger's snowboard production capacity by 150,000 boards annually to 230,000, the statement said. Scott also planned to promote Blizzard racing skis and its new "carve skis", which aim to rival snowboards.
Mittersill will become a European development centre for Scott winter sports goods.
Raiffeisenverband rescued Blizzard from the brink of bankruptcy in August last year and immediately began searching for a buyer for the firm.
"Thanks to a successful restructuring programme in Mittersill over the past 12 months, a successful company has developed that is fit for the future," Raiffeisen said.
It forecast Blizzard would at least break even in 1996/7.
Austrian media have put the sale price for Blizzard Holding B&H VerwaltungsGmbH and operative units Blizzard MarketingGmbH and High Tech ProduktionsGmbH at 50-90 million schillings.
-- Janet McBride, Vienna Newsroom 43-1-531 12 254 ($ = 10.71 Austrian Schillings)
